topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture series, outlines student expectations across disciplines, and presents the session's key learning objectives.

topics.label: Biological basis of cancer as a failure of differentiation and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: They describe cancer as a disruption of cellular differentiation and three-dimensional tissue organization caused by accumulated alterations, along with experimental models used to study these properties.

topics.label: Distinguishing benign from malignant tumors through invasion and metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: They explore how tumors are evaluated as benign or malignant based on tissue invasion and metastatic spread, using gross anatomy, histology, and stepwise colorectal progression as examples.

topics.label: Conventions and exceptions of tumor nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the standard suffix rules and notable clinical exceptions used to name tumors based on their tissue of origin and malignant potential.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: It details the physical obstructions, organ failures, and systemic complications through which primary and metastatic tumors cause illness and death.

topics.label: Tumor incidence across human populations and multicellular species
topics.groupedBecause: They compare tumor frequencies across human organs and diverse animal taxa, demonstrating that cancer is an inherent risk across multicellular organisms.

topics.label: Clinical screening modalities and early tumor detection
topics.groupedBecause: They evaluate the rationale, histological criteria, and practical utility of population-based screening programs for detecting precursor lesions before malignancy develops.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: It wraps up the lecture with concluding remarks, a reminder of the learning outcomes, and notice of upcoming practical sessions.
